learning_outcomes.text: Understand the main issues related to the design and operation of mechanical components.
Acquire the ability to schematize and quantize structural problems.

Address issues related to the exercise of mechanical components, with particular reference to axes and trees, illustrating problems of static and dynamic strength, fatigue, ductile and brittle materials, and wear.
Acquire the foundation needed to address engineering problems by applying scientific knowledge acquired in previous courses.
Identify major structural problems related to the exercise of mechanical components.
Identify the most dangerous working conditions.
Perform a critical analysis of the structural solution.
Understand the reasons who determined the achieved solutions.
Analyze technical documents on the topics of the course.
Express the result of calculations in the form of a technical report.
Be able to fully illustrate by sketches, calculations, text, the problems inherent in the various structural solutions.

syllabus_topics: Notes on the analysis of loads in structural testing
Materials: Properties of cast iron, steel, other metal alloys, plastics, composites
Stress states: Tension, compression, bending, shear and torsion
Euler's formula for elastic instability of beams
Yield of components: maximum normal stress, maximum shear stress, maximum energy of distortion, Mohr-Coulomb and modified Mohr approach
High and low cycle Fatigue: principal factors affecting life, Complex states of stress, cumulative damage
Surface damage: Corrosion, Stress corrosion cracking, Fatigue and corrosion
teaching_methods: Practical design problems solutions with teacher/tutor support
Integration with auxiliary material (manuals, commercial catalogues, laws, videos of laboratory tests, web tools)
assessment_rules: The examination consists of a written and an oral test. The written test involves solving problems similar to those faced in the course, requiring identification of loads and constraints and initial component sizing. The oral test focuses on course topics, verifying concepts related to sizing and monitoring of mechanical components.
bibliography: R.C. Juvinal, K.M.Marshek - "Fundamentals of Machine Components Design", Wiley
J.E. Shigley, R.G. Budynas, J.K. Nisbett, " Shigley’s Mechanichal Engineering Design". McGraw-Hill
degree: Laurea in Ingegneria Meccanica E Gestionale (First Level Degree In Mechanical And Management Engineering), classe L-9 Classe delle lauree in Ingegneria industriale
